bug_semantics: A STOMP client authenticated with only SEND or CONSUME permission could request a routing type that an existing address did not support. STOMP's auto-create path added that routing type by calling the broker server's updateAddressInfo directly, without the ServerSession CREATE_ADDRESS authorization check; the subsequent routing-semantics check then observed the newly added type and accepted the send or subscription. This let a low-privilege user mutate address routing configuration despite lacking createAddress permission.
flaw_origin: Commit d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 added the first existing-address/missing-routing-type branch to StompConnection.autoCreateDestinationIfPossible. It copied the address's routing types, added the client-requested effectiveAddressRoutingType, and invoked manager.getServer().updateAddressInfo(...) directly. The parent only auto-created through the authenticated ServerSession when an address did not exist and otherwise left an unsupported routing type for checkRoutingSemantics to reject. Later edits moved or modernized the same sink but did not originate the authorization bypass.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 shows human author Justin Bertram <jbertram@apache.org>, human committer Clebert Suconic <clebertsuconic@apache.org>, a one-line ARTEMIS-1794 message, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer/marker.
evidence: The assigned GHSA/CVE advisory describes the authorization failure for org.apache.artemis:artemis-stomp-protocol and identifies Apache PR https://github.com/apache/artemis/pull/6395 plus commit 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474; its published boundary is vulnerable through 2.53.0 and first patched in 2.54.0.

At fix parent 845339b1b66ecd7eac3dc07351cda850ee476d56, artemis-protocols/artemis-stomp-protocol/src/main/java/org/apache/activemq/artemis/core/protocol/stomp/StompConnection.java:191-198 detects an existing address missing effectiveAddressRoutingType, adds the type to an EnumSet, and calls manager.getServer().updateAddressInfo directly. VersionedStompFrameHandler.java:190-198 invokes this path before STOMP SEND, while StompConnection.java:545-556 invokes it before SUBSCRIBE.

git show 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474 removes autoCreateDestinationIfPossible and routes both SEND and SUBSCRIBE through StompConnection.checkAutoCreate, which calls getSession().getCoreSession().checkAutoCreate. At that commit ServerSessionImpl.checkAutoCreate updates a missing routing type through createAddress, and ServerSessionImpl.java:1005-1012 performs securityCheck(..., CheckType.CREATE_ADDRESS, this) before addOrUpdateAddressInfo. The added StompWithSecurityTest cases require ERROR AMQ229032 for send-only and consume-only users requesting MULTICAST on an ANYCAST address and assert that MULTICAST remains absent.

git log -S'updateAddressInfo(simpleQueue, routingTypes)' identifies d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 as the 2018-04-10 origin and ede2051960ddd6bf5657076fe5889f18a5699c6c as a later 2020 refactor; git log -L over the vulnerable method likewise traces the existing-address augmentation branch to d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69. In that BIC, StompConnection.java:296-297 contains routingTypes.add(effectiveAddressRoutingType) followed by updateAddressInfo.

Direct parent-tree verification: d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 has the single parent e937c9903f9fa429c23fe50a3fd49e99ad2de0b9, and git grep at that exact parent finds neither updateAddressInfo nor routingTypes.add(effectiveAddressRoutingType) in StompConnection.java. The BIC diff shows the parent only handled addressInfo == null; unsupported types on existing addresses therefore reached checkRoutingSemantics and were rejected.

Version boundary verification: git grep finds no updateAddressInfo sink in StompConnection.java at tag 2.5.0, finds it at 2.6.0:297 and 2.53.0:197, finds it absent at 2.54.0, and finds the authenticated getCoreSession().checkAutoCreate call at 2.54.0:514. git tag --contains places d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 first in 2.6.0 and places fix 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474 first in 2.54.0. ASF JIRA ARTEMIS-1794 also records the BIC feature's fix version as 2.6.0.

The GHSA's broad lower range begins at 2.0.0, but direct source inspection at tag 2.0.0 shows autoCreateDestinationIfPossible only creates through ServerSession when the address is absent and checkRoutingSemantics rejects a requested type missing from an existing address; the direct server update branch does not appear until 2.6.0. This is a documented advisory-range overbreadth, not evidence for an earlier BIC of this exact flaw.

BIC-only AI inspection used git cat-file -p d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69. The commit object contains ordinary human author/committer identities and no trailers or AI markers; PR bodies, the 2026 fix, and later commits were not used for AI attribution.
reasoning: The vulnerability is the authorization bypass in the existing-address routing-type augmentation, not generic STOMP auto-creation. Before the BIC, STOMP could auto-create a missing address through ServerSession (and its security boundary), but it did not mutate an existing address to satisfy a mismatched routing type; checkRoutingSemantics rejected that request. ARTEMIS-1794 commit d773e8f66b5db2b0fcaa646384c24690d38aaa69 deliberately enabled two STOMP routing types on the same address and introduced the smallest causal branch: it directly changed the broker's AddressInfo outside ServerSession authorization. The exact sink is absent from its immediate parent and is present beginning with release 2.6.0. Later refactors retain the same mechanism, so they are not introducers. ARTEMIS-5996 commit 53173375c4d5e4b57890e89d37ed8b666c974474 is the direct fix: it deletes the duplicated STOMP mutation logic and sends both attack paths through ServerSession.checkAutoCreate, whose createAddress path enforces CREATE_ADDRESS; its regression tests cover both send-only and consume-only credentials, and it lands in the first patched tag 2.54.0 after the sink remains in 2.53.0. Although the advisory conservatively lists versions back to 2.0.0, tag-level code establishes that this exact flaw begins in 2.6.0. Finally, the BIC commit object has no AI authorship or generation marker, so the causal result is NOT_AI.
